summary: Port reproduces the original's 30-function easing library exactly — same curves to sub-pixel accuracy, same order, same 5.00 s cadence, same 150 s loop — but draws every curve vertically MIRRORED against the (unmirrored) linear reference diagonal, omits the original's red demo dot on the middle row, and runs its white eased marker 2.5x too slow.
observations: Rig: 16x16 grid, 256 px, no controls on EITHER side (probe: 'no settable controls' for orig and port) — control surfaces match, so dials are not a factor.

Both sides draw the same three-element scene: a dim gray linear reference line along y=x, a full-hue-wheel curve (red at x=0 -> yellow -> green -> cyan -> blue -> magenta -> red at x=15) plotting the current easing function, and a white eased marker that sweeps the strip index in raster order (index i drawn at x=i%16, y=floor(i/16)).

EASING LIBRARY MATCHES EXACTLY. Sampling the mid-frame of every 5 s mode across 240 s (48 samples), the port's per-column curve profile equals 15 minus the original's to within 0.16-0.68 px mean error at EVERY sample. Mode changes happen at the same instant on both sides (--dump at 4.80/4.85/4.90/4.95 s: both switch between 4.90 and 4.95 s). The whole sequence is 30 functions x 5.00 s and repeats with a 150 s period on both sides (profile at t=152 s is byte-identical to t=2 s, 157 s to 7 s, ... on the original, and the port tracks it).

DIVERGENCE 1 - curve is vertically mirrored. The gray reference diagonal is drawn as y=x on BOTH sides, but the original's ease curve also runs top-left -> bottom-right (same sense as the reference, so curve and reference nearly coincide and you read the ease as a bow away from linear), while the port's runs bottom-left -> top-right and CROSSES the reference in an X. Exact: at t=0 s orig per-column curve centroid y = 0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,1.5,2.0,3.0,4.0,5.0,6.5,7.5,9.0,10.5,12.0,13.5,14.5; port = 15.0,14.5,14.5,14.5,13.5,13.0,12.5,11.5,10.0,8.5,7.5,6.5,4.5,3.5,1.5,0.0. This holds in every mode over 240 s.

DIVERGENCE 2 - missing red demo dot. The original also draws a pure red (255,0,0) dot that ping-pongs horizontally along the middle row y=8, x=0 <-> 15, with visibly eased (accelerating/decelerating) velocity and in phase with the white marker: t=0 s x=0, t=0.4 s x=3-4, t=0.6 s x=7, t=0.8 s x=12, t=1.0 s x=14, t=1.4 s x=5-6, t=1.8 s x=0-1. Scanning every dumped frame of the port (0-20 s at 0.2 s, plus 0-2 s at 0.05 s, plus 48 samples over 240 s), the port's ONLY pure-red pixels are the curve's own endpoints at (15,0) and (0,15) — it never draws this second marker.

DIVERGENCE 3 - white marker 2.5x too slow. Tracking the marker's mean strip index: original sweeps 0 -> 255 -> 0 with a 2.00 s round trip (troughs at t=0,2,4 s, peaks at 1,3 s; autocorrelation of the motion series peaks at lag 40 frames = 2.00 s at 20 fps). Port takes 5.00 s for the same round trip (index 1 at t=0, 248 at 2.4 s, 2 at 4.8 s; 1 at 10.0 s, 255 at 12.4 s, 1 at 15.0 s) — exactly one round trip per easing mode instead of 2.5, and its motion autocorrelation shows only the 5.00 s mode peak, no 2 s peak.
DIVERGENCE 4 - reference line dimmer. The gray diagonal is 76/76/76 on the original and 50/50/50 on the port.

DIVERGENCE 5 - curve stroke slightly thinner. Counting curve-only lit pixels (excluding gray line and white marker) per frame across 8 different modes: orig 31-39 (typically 2-3 px per column), port 25-30 (typically 1-2 px per column); the port occasionally leaves a column with zero curve pixels (e.g. t=35 s, column 15). Net effect over 240 s: mean brightness 21 (orig) vs 16 (port), and zeroMotionFrames 5/480 vs 17/480.
Both sides are healthy otherwise: no compile or runtime errors, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both in the 6 s, 240 s and skip-200 s/30 s windows; neither binds sensors.

Both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: marker phase at fixed absolute times is unchanged across --fps 10/20/40 on BOTH sides (e.g. orig index at t=2.0 s = 4/1/1, port = 193/185/181), so there is no frame-rate-coupling divergence.
Both sides are seed-independent: seed 1234 renders identical curve profiles and marker phase to seed 1 at t=1, 6 and 11 s.
feedback: Flip the plotted curve vertically. The port currently draws the ease at y = 15 - origY for every column and every mode; the linear reference diagonal it draws (y=x) is already correct, so only the curve is inverted. After the fix the ease curve should run corner-to-corner in the SAME direction as the gray reference (top-left to bottom-right) and hug it, rather than crossing it in an X.

Add the missing second marker: a pure red (255,0,0) dot on the horizontal centre row (y=8 on a 16x16 grid), positioned at the same eased value as the white marker, ping-ponging x=0 <-> 15 in phase with it. It is one to two pixels wide and is the most legible 'what does this easing feel like' element in the original.

Speed the white eased marker up by 2.5x: the original completes a full out-and-back sweep of the strip index in 2.00 s, so there are 2.5 round trips inside each 5 s easing mode; the port currently takes 5.00 s, exactly one round trip per mode.
Brighten the gray linear reference from 50/50/50 to 76/76/76.

Thicken the curve stroke slightly — the original lays down 2-3 pixels per column (31-39 curve pixels per frame), the port 1-2 (25-30), and the port sometimes drops a column entirely (t=35 s, column 15). Filling the vertical gap between adjacent column samples so no column is empty would close most of the difference.

Everything else is already right and should not be touched: the 30-function library, its order, the 5.00 s per-function cadence and switch instants, the 150 s loop, the hue mapping along x, the raster index mapping of the white marker, and the time-based (fps-invariant) clock.
